page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor, specifically the Neoverse-N1 model. This instance features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. It does not contain local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across multi-core compute and memory bandwidth workloads. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 12130.94 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5435.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 472.59 GB/sec for cached reads and 119.78 GB/sec for uncached reads. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 946.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.79. Cryptographic performance is a notable bottleneck, as evidenced by a poor Passmark CPU encryption score of 1082.7. Text processing and compression tasks also rank in the lower percentiles, with gzip compression single-threaded throughput at 20.35 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c6gn.2xlarge utilizes ARM-based architecture to deliver balanced multi-threaded performance and high network throughput without the premium associated with x86 hardware. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for network-intensive, compute-bound workloads. It is optimized for tasks such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 9.68 GB/sec, and database operations, processing 9.2 million Redis SET operations per second. It is also applicable for software compilation and physics simulations. Conversely, it is poorly suited for memory-heavy databases, large-scale LLM inference, or workloads requiring advanced vector or matrix instruction sets.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.2xlarge is a compute-optimized, network-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 ARMv8 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB per core, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Benchmarks show average multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5435.0 and 9.2 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core and cryptographic performance are weak. The instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for ARM-compatible workloads, making it suitable for static web serving, software compilation, and database operations that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high network throughput rather than massive memory capacity.
